title: The effect of using virtual reality headsets during minimally invasive adrenal vein blood sampling for endocrinological sampling - a randomized controlled pilot study
summary:
Primary hyperaldosteronism is the cause of treatment-resistant high blood pressure in 3-15% of patients. Adrenal vein blood sampling is the gold standard for differentiating between unilateral and bilateral aldosterone overproduction. A catheter is inserted via the groin to various locations in the venous system, including the adrenal veins, and blood is taken for hormone determination - patients are usually awake during this procedure, which can cause stress, anxiety and pain.

Virtual reality (VR) headsets allow patients to be distracted from their surroundings by audiovisual stimuli and are already being used successfully to reduce pain and anxiety. Studies on the use of VR during adrenal vein blood sampling do not yet exist.

The aim of this study is to investigate the influence of VR goggles on anxiety, pain, hemodynamic parameters, examination duration, radiation exposure and cortisol level as an objective stress marker during the examination.

interventions.name: Adrenal vein blood sampling (AVBS) with VR headset

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinically indicated selective adrenal vein blood sampling
- signed study consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindication for clinically indicated selective adrenal vein blood sampling
- Patient age under 18 years
- Migraine with aura
- Claustrophobia
- Epilepsy
- Severe balance disorder
- Kinetosis
- Acute psychosis
